answer: Bonded escrows make identities costly to operate: when k coordinated keys equivocate, correlated evidence triggers aggregate slashing proportional to k², not k separate linear fines. As the tide of evidence exposes repeated offenses, asymmetric capital depreciation compounds losses across rounds, so a controller cannot cheaply forge a swarm, split stake, or wander between identities; the capital-loss multiplier grows exponentially across detected rounds, making sybil coordination economically irrational.
